```plato
    // A helper taking an interface-typed first parameter cannot be called on a
    // interface-typed value from inside another body: the writer monomorphizes it
    // per concrete type and no overload accepts the interface (the same shape
    // LINT013 reports as an unreachable derived surface). So the path tangent and
    // the base-surface normal below are written out at each of their three call
    // sites rather than factored out. Only obligations — `Eval` here — dispatch
    // through an interface.

    // The same restriction bites one step further out: a helper whose first parameter
    // is a CONCRETE INSTANTIATION of a generic type (`net: Array2D<Point3D>`) is not
    // monomorphized into an extension either, so the call sites read the control net's
    // ColumnCount (U direction) and RowCount (V direction) fields directly. There is
    // nothing to factor out — both were one-line field reads.

    //==
    // Patches and control nets

    // Bilinear interpolation of the four corners: lerp along U on each V edge,
    // then lerp between those two results along V.
    Eval(s: BilinearPatch, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D
        => s.P00.Lerp(s.P10, uv.U).Lerp(s.P01.Lerp(s.P11, uv.U), uv.V);
```

```plato
    // The tensor-product de Casteljau: reduce each row of the control net along
    // U, then reduce the resulting column of points along V.
    Eval(s: BezierPatch, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D
        => s.ControlPoints.RowCount
            .MapRange(r => s.ControlPoints.Row(r).DeCasteljau(uv.U))
            .DeCasteljau(uv.V);
```

```plato
    // The tensor-product B-spline sum: each control point weighted by the
    // product of its U and V basis functions (splines.library.plato).
    // The unit UV parameters are mapped onto the two knot domains first.
    Eval(s: BSplineSurface, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D {
        var uDomain = s.UKnots.Domain(s.UDegree);
        var vDomain = s.VKnots.Domain(s.VDegree);
        var u = KnotParameter(uDomain, uv.U);
        var v = KnotParameter(vDomain, uv.V);
        var columns = s.ControlPoints.ColumnCount;
        var sum = s.ControlPoints.Count.Range.Reduce(Vector3D.Zero, (acc, k) =>
            acc + s.ControlPoints.Row(k / columns)[k % columns].PositionVector
                * (BasisFunction(s.UKnots, uDomain.End, k % columns, s.UDegree, u)
                   * BasisFunction(s.VKnots, vDomain.End, k / columns, s.VDegree, v)));
        return (sum.X, sum.Y, sum.Z);
    }
```

```plato

    // The rational form: the same tensor-product sum over weight-scaled control
    // points, divided by the summed weighted basis — the projection out of
    // homogeneous space that lets a NURBS surface hold a quadric exactly.
    Eval(s: NurbsSurface, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D {
        var uDomain = s.UKnots.Domain(s.UDegree);
        var vDomain = s.VKnots.Domain(s.VDegree);
        var u = KnotParameter(uDomain, uv.U);
        var v = KnotParameter(vDomain, uv.V);
        var columns = s.ControlPoints.ColumnCount;
        var count = s.ControlPoints.Count;
        var numerator = count.Range.Reduce(Vector3D.Zero, (acc, k) =>
            acc + s.ControlPoints.Row(k / columns)[k % columns].PositionVector
                * (s.Weights.Row(k / columns)[k % columns]
                   * BasisFunction(s.UKnots, uDomain.End, k % columns, s.UDegree, u)
                   * BasisFunction(s.VKnots, vDomain.End, k / columns, s.VDegree, v)));
        var denominator = count.Range.Reduce(0.0, (acc, k) =>
            acc + s.Weights.Row(k / columns)[k % columns]
                * BasisFunction(s.UKnots, uDomain.End, k % columns, s.UDegree, u)
                * BasisFunction(s.VKnots, vDomain.End, k / columns, s.VDegree, v));
        var p = denominator == 0.0 ? numerator : numerator / denominator;
        return (p.X, p.Y, p.Z);
    }
```

```plato
    // The Coons blend: the two ruled surfaces between opposite boundary pairs,
    // minus the bilinear patch on the four corners that both of them contain.
    // Point3D is IInterpolatable but not IAdditive, so the subtraction is spelled
    // through the point difference — `bilinear + (ruledV - bilinear)` — which is
    // exactly what `Between` gives and needs no new interface.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coons_patch
    Eval(s: CoonsPatch, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D {
        var ruledV = s.Bottom.Eval(uv.U).Lerp(s.Top.Eval(uv.U), uv.V);
        var ruledU = s.Left.Eval(uv.V).Lerp(s.Right.Eval(uv.V), uv.U);
        var corners = s.Bottom.Eval(0.0).Lerp(s.Bottom.Eval(1.0), uv.U)
            .Lerp(s.Top.Eval(0.0).Lerp(s.Top.Eval(1.0), uv.U), uv.V);
        return ruledV + corners.Between(ruledU);
    }
```

```plato
    // A latitude/longitude window: U sweeps the azimuth interval, V the
    // inclination interval (measured from the sphere's +Z pole).
    Eval(s: SphericalPatch, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D
    {
        var azimuth = s.Azimuths.Lerp(uv.U);
        var inclination = s.Inclinations.Lerp(uv.V);
        var r = s.Sphere.Radius;
        return (s.Sphere.Center.X + inclination.Sin * azimuth.Cos * r,
                s.Sphere.Center.Y + inclination.Sin * azimuth.Sin * r,
                s.Sphere.Center.Z + inclination.Cos * r);
    }
```

```plato

    //==
    // Generated surfaces

    // The profile lifted into the axis frame and turned: U sweeps the angle
    // interval, V follows the profile. The profile's X is the radial distance
    // from the axis and its Y the distance along it, so the point is the axis
    // origin plus a radial offset in the plane orthogonal to the axis plus an
    // axial offset. Which perpendicular starts the sweep is arbitrary — the
    // surface is the same set either way — so it is chosen deterministically.
    Eval(s: SurfaceOfRevolution, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D {
        var angle = s.Angles.Lerp(uv.U);
        var profile = s.Profile.Eval(uv.V);
        var axis = s.Axis.Direction.Vector;
        var e1 = AnyPerpendicular(axis);
        var e2 = axis.Cross(e1);
        return s.Axis.Origin
             + e1 * (profile.X * angle.Cos)
             + e2 * (profile.X * angle.Sin)
             + axis * profile.Y;
    }
```

```plato
    // The profile translated along Direction by V * Distance.
    Eval(s: ExtrudedSurface, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D
    {
        var p = s.Profile.Eval(uv.U);
        var d = s.Direction.Vector;
        var k = s.Distance * uv.V;
        return (p.X + d.X * k, p.Y + d.Y * k, p.Z + d.Z * k);
    }
```

```plato
    // U runs around each section, V across the stack: the two bracketing
    // sections sampled at u and blended. A closed loft wraps the last section
    // back to the first, which is the extra span its Closed flag buys.
    Eval(s: LoftedSurface, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D {
        var count = s.Sections.Count;
        var spans = (s.Closed ? count : count - 1).Max(1);
        var t = uv.V.Clamp(0.0, 1.0) * spans.ToNumber;
        var j = t.Floor.ToInteger.Max(0).Min(spans - 1);
        return SectionPoint(s.Sections[j % count], uv.U)
            .Lerp(SectionPoint(s.Sections[(j + 1) % count], uv.U), t - j.ToNumber);
    }
```

## Line 241

```plato

    // The 2D profile carried along the path: U follows the profile, V the path.
    // Approximation (see the file header): the cross-section frame is the path
    // tangent plus a deterministic perpendicular, not the rotation-minimizing
    // frame, so the section can twist relative to a true sweep where the path
    // turns about its own tangent. The tangent is a central difference with its
    // sample parameters clamped, so the ends see a one-sided difference.
    Eval(s: SweptSurface, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D {
        var h = ParameterStep();
        var origin = s.Path.Eval(uv.V);
        var tangent = s.Path.Eval((uv.V - h).Clamp(0.0, 1.0))
            .Between(s.Path.Eval((uv.V + h).Clamp(0.0, 1.0))).Normalize;
        var e1 = AnyPerpendicular(tangent);
        var e2 = tangent.Cross(e1);
        var profile = s.Profile.Eval(uv.U);
        return origin + e1 * profile.X + e2 * profile.Y;
    }
```

## Line 260

**Source:** [stdlib/geometry/surfaces.library.plato, line 260](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/surfaces.library.plato#L260).

```plato

    // A circle of radius Radius held normal to the path: U goes once around the
    // circle, V along the path. Same frame approximation as SweptSurface, and it
    // matters less here — a circular section is invariant under the twist the
    // fixed-up frame introduces.
    Eval(s: TubeSurface, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D {
        var h = ParameterStep();
        var origin = s.Path.Eval(uv.V);
        var tangent = s.Path.Eval((uv.V - h).Clamp(0.0, 1.0))
            .Between(s.Path.Eval((uv.V + h).Clamp(0.0, 1.0))).Normalize;
        var e1 = AnyPerpendicular(tangent);
        var e2 = tangent.Cross(e1);
        var around = uv.U.Turns;
        return origin + e1 * (s.Radius * around.Cos) + e2 * (s.Radius * around.Sin);
    }
```

## Line 278

**Source:** [stdlib/geometry/surfaces.library.plato, line 278](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/surfaces.library.plato#L278).

```plato

    // The base point displaced along the base normal by Distance. The normal is
    // a central difference of the base's own evaluation, because
    // `IParametricSurface` exposes no derivative (only `IDifferentiableSurface`
    // does); the sample parameters are clamped, so the boundary gets a one-sided
    // difference rather than an off-surface point.
    Eval(s: OffsetSurface, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D {
        var h = ParameterStep();
        var alongU = s.Base.Eval(UvCoordinate((uv.U - h).Clamp(0.0, 1.0), uv.V))
            .Between(s.Base.Eval(UvCoordinate((uv.U + h).Clamp(0.0, 1.0), uv.V)));
        var alongV = s.Base.Eval(UvCoordinate(uv.U, (uv.V - h).Clamp(0.0, 1.0)))
            .Between(s.Base.Eval(UvCoordinate(uv.U, (uv.V + h).Clamp(0.0, 1.0))));
        return s.Base.Eval(uv) + alongU.Cross(alongV).Normalize * s.Distance;
    }
```

## Line 295

```plato

    //==
    // Height fields

    // The elevation at a ground position: the bilinear blend of the four
    // surrounding samples, clamped to the edge outside Domain. Columns run along
    // X and rows along Y, and the samples sit at the corners of the sample grid,
    // so a Heights array of c columns spans c - 1 intervals across Domain.
    Eval(s: HeightField, position: Point2D): Number {
        var columns = s.Heights.ColumnCount;
        var rows = s.Heights.RowCount;
        var min = s.Domain.Min;
        var max = s.Domain.Max;
        var x = max.X == min.X ? 0.0 : (position.X - min.X) / (max.X - min.X) * (columns - 1).ToNumber;
        var y = max.Y == min.Y ? 0.0 : (position.Y - min.Y) / (max.Y - min.Y) * (rows - 1).ToNumber;
        var i = x.Floor.ToInteger;
        var j = y.Floor.ToInteger;
        return s.SampleAt(i, j).Lerp(s.SampleAt(i + 1, j), x - x.Floor)
            .Lerp(s.SampleAt(i, j + 1).Lerp(s.SampleAt(i + 1, j + 1), x - x.Floor), y - y.Floor);
    }
```

## Line 322

**Source:** [stdlib/geometry/surfaces.library.plato, line 322](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/surfaces.library.plato#L322).

```plato

    //==
    // Topological surfaces

    // One lap of the centerline circle in U, across the strip in V. The strip's
    // half-width direction rotates by HalfTwistCount half-turns over the lap, so
    // an odd count returns the strip to its start flipped: the one-sided surface.
    Eval(s: MobiusStrip, uv: UvCoordinate): Point3D
    {
        var lap = uv.U.Turns;
        var twist = (uv.U * s.HalfTwistCount.ToNumber * 0.5).Turns;
        var w = (uv.V - 0.5) * s.Width;
        var ring = s.Radius + w * twist.Cos;
        return s.Frame.PointInFrame(Point3D(ring * lap.Cos, ring * lap.Sin, w * twist.Sin));
    }
```
